ecosystemRotation: dependency/workflow integrity, CI security, and process isolation

candidates.architecture: official Node runtime selected by actions/setup-node
candidates.harvest: pin exact LTS patch in verification workflows while retaining package engine >=24 for user runtime compatibility
candidates.expectedBenefit: remove semver drift between identical Ferrum commits and make failures/runtime evidence reproducible
candidates.platformCoverage: Linux and Windows Ferrum CI plus all Node-backed companion workflows
candidates.compatibilityRisks: exact CI pin requires deliberate update when a materially better 24.x patch is proven
candidates.upstreamIssues: none material found for current Ferrum acceptance surface
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: proposal exact head has all affected gates green except one still-running Tauri Ubuntu official-reference job
candidates.smallestExperiment: same complete Ferrum workflow surface with floating 24 replaced only by 24.19.0
candidates.acceptanceTest: all affected exact-head workflows successful with no target/evidence regression
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: pending Tauri job completes or fails; newer Node 24 patch with relevant fixes

candidates.releaseOrHead: npm 11 documentation; Ferrum Node pin bundles npm 11.17.0
candidates.architecture: npm CLI verification of downloaded package registry signatures and Sigstore provenance attestations
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: dependency integrity after frozen npm ci
candidates.harvest: machine-readable verified signature/attestation counts and failure attribution
candidates.expectedBenefit: detect tampered or invalidly attested downloaded packages beyond lockfile integrity
candidates.compatibilityRisks: npm docs recommend latest CLI for evolving attestation formats; Node-bundled npm may lag
candidates.upstreamIssues: verification availability depends on registry/package signing
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: official npm command verifies registry signatures and provenance attestations
candidates.smallestExperiment: run npm audit signatures after clean npm ci and capture JSON/attestation counts, then plant a controlled invalid package fixture if feasible
candidates.acceptanceTest: bounded overhead, deterministic structured output, real integrity signal not already provided by lockfile npm ci
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Node/npm pin merges or npm attestation format/version changes

candidates.architecture: static package-lock/yarn lock validation for allowed hosts, HTTPS, package name/resolved URL and integrity
candidates.harvest: fail fast on planted registry host/scheme/name/integrity defects before install
candidates.expectedBenefit: detect lockfile trust defects that npm ci alone may not classify clearly
candidates.compatibilityRisks: additional dependency and policy maintenance; must avoid false positives on legitimate lock entries
candidates.upstreamIssues: must prove support for Ferrum package-lock v3 shape
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: maintained tool with explicit lockfile security policies
candidates.smallestExperiment: clone Ferrum lockfile into four planted wrong-host/http/name/integrity fixtures
candidates.acceptanceTest: catch every planted defect, pass canonical lockfile, negligible CI overhead, no network requirement if possible
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: canonical package-lock changes or planted-fixture experiment completed

candidates.architecture: lockfile/SBOM scanner backed by OSV data with offline database support
candidates.harvest: separate vulnerability evidence from lockfile-integrity evidence
candidates.expectedBenefit: current vulnerability classification without altering install/runtime behavior
candidates.compatibilityRisks: database freshness/network cost and advisory noise; remediation mode can execute package managers and is out of scope initially
candidates.upstreamIssues: none material to read-only scanning identified
candidates.smallestExperiment: scan current lockfile in read-only JSON mode and measure actionable findings and overhead
candidates.acceptanceTest: machine-readable useful signal with bounded time and zero mutation
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: dependency/security incident or lockfile scanner experiment rotation

candidates.purpose: dependency supply-chain analysis and MCP auditability
candidates.architecture: CLI/MCP security tooling with package-integrity and structured audit features
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: agent-facing audit logs and dependency integrity
candidates.harvest: append-only structured tool-execution audit pattern and explicit cache-poisoning hardening ideas
candidates.integrationMode: TRANSPLANT-IDEA; external service integration only after separate proof
candidates.expectedBenefit: more attributable agent operations and better dependency-risk context
candidates.requiredDependencies: Socket CLI/service credentials for full features
candidates.compatibilityRisks: external service/token dependency and overlapping Ferrum evidence model
candidates.upstreamIssues: service coupling makes direct default dependency unattractive
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: current head adds structured JSON MCP audit logging and project has package-integrity checks
candidates.smallestExperiment: compare Ferrum native evidence envelope with Socket audit fields on one fixed agent workflow
candidates.acceptanceTest: material attribution improvement without duplicating or obscuring raw Ferrum evidence
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Ferrum agent audit schema work or major Socket local/offline capability change

candidates.architecture: workflow/action semantic security linter with audits for injection, cache poisoning, permissions, credential persistence and related hazards
candidates.harvest: independent detection of workflow security/determinism regressions such as accidental cache reintroduction
candidates.expectedBenefit: catch dangerous workflow changes before they reach exact-head acceptance
candidates.compatibilityRisks: false positives and tool itself must be pinned to a safe release; v1.27.0 had a credential logging defect fixed afterward
candidates.upstreamIssues: audit policy needs Ferrum-specific allowlist rather than blanket suppression
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: current releases include cache-poisoning and ad-hoc-package audits; project dogfoods pinned zizmor action
candidates.smallestExperiment: run v1.29.0 against current .github and plant one known unsafe cache/permission fixture
candidates.acceptanceTest: canonical workflows clean or explainable; planted defect reliably found; low runtime overhead
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: PR60 workflow work converges or zizmor security release

candidates.purpose: GitHub Actions syntax and semantic validation
candidates.architecture: static workflow linter with expression/schema/shellcheck integrations
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: workflow correctness before expensive runtime gates
candidates.harvest: fast structural validation complementary to zizmor security analysis
candidates.expectedBenefit: fail faster on workflow/schema mistakes before hosted runtime matrices
candidates.compatibilityRisks: GitHub schema changes can temporarily cause false positives
candidates.upstreamIssues: must verify current Actions v7 inputs and Ferrum dynamic expressions
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: current release supports modern schedule timezone validation and signed/checksummed binaries
candidates.smallestExperiment: lint every Ferrum workflow and compare runtime to full CI feedback
candidates.acceptanceTest: zero unexplained false positives and meaningful pre-runtime defect detection under a few seconds
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: next workflow change or actionlint release

candidates.purpose: runtime hardening and outbound/network observation for GitHub-hosted runners
candidates.architecture: runner hardening action with runtime policy/telemetry
candidates.harvest: observe unexpected dependency/tool network endpoints before enforcing policy
candidates.expectedBenefit: detect compromised or surprising CI egress without reducing test fidelity
candidates.compatibilityRisks: network enforcement can break legitimate dynamic test traffic; external service coupling
candidates.upstreamIssues: must prove compatibility with browser downloads, GitHub wiki probes, Appium, Tauri and attestation paths
candidates.smallestExperiment: observe-only on one narrow unit/security workflow before any enforcement
candidates.acceptanceTest: complete endpoint inventory, negligible overhead, zero test breakage
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: zizmor/actionlint experiment completes or workflow supply-chain incident

candidates.purpose: rootless process isolation for agent-executed workloads
candidates.architecture: Rust process sandbox using Landlock, seccomp-bpf/seccomp user notification, COW filesystem, network/HTTP policy and resource controls
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: process/CLI/service target isolation and deterministic execution
candidates.harvest: explicit effective policy, no-network/read-only/COW controls, deterministic time/random and low-startup-cost isolation
candidates.expectedBenefit: contain untrusted app/test workloads while preserving Ferrum lifecycle/evidence contracts
candidates.requiredDependencies: Linux kernel capabilities; Linux 6.12+ for full Landlock ABI v6 protection; Sandlock binary
candidates.compatibilityRisks: shared host kernel, feature level varies by kernel, policy complexity; protections must fail closed when requested
candidates.upstreamIssues: young project; selective protection waivers must never silently weaken Ferrum's requested policy
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: upstream reports about 5 ms startup and exposes machine-readable effective configuration
candidates.smallestExperiment: same Ferrum process/service fixture unisolated versus strict no-network/read-only/resource-bounded Sandlock
candidates.acceptanceTest: functional/evidence parity, denied operations demonstrably fail, requested protections active, bounded median/p95 overhead
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Node/STATUS work converges or Sandlock kernel/support model materially changes

candidates.architecture: Linux namespaces, resource limits/cgroups and seccomp/Kafel policy
candidates.expectedBenefit: stronger established Linux isolation comparator against lighter Sandlock
candidates.requiredDependencies: Linux namespaces and nsjail build/runtime dependencies
candidates.compatibilityRisks: heavier configuration and setup than Sandlock; privilege/kernel constraints
candidates.upstreamIssues: must not make CI/application testing depend on unavailable namespace features
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: long-lived Google project, active current head
candidates.smallestExperiment: same strict Ferrum process workload as Sandlock with equivalent filesystem/network restrictions
candidates.acceptanceTest: parity plus enforcement and measured startup/action overhead
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Sandlock experiment yields a credible isolation benefit

candidates.architecture: user/mount/PID/IPC/network namespace construction with explicit filesystem bindings
candidates.harvest: small policy surface and explicit filesystem exposure model
candidates.expectedBenefit: lower-complexity containment where namespace primitives are sufficient
candidates.compatibilityRisks: lower-level policy burden; current head includes a deliberate fail-open --not-a-security-boundary option that Ferrum must never use for security isolation
candidates.upstreamIssues: security boundary depends on caller configuration; no Ferrum-level evidence contract
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: widely used by Flatpak/desktop sandboxing ecosystems
candidates.smallestExperiment: same process fixture with read-only source, writable temp and no network
candidates.acceptanceTest: restrictions demonstrably enforced with no hidden fail-open behavior and acceptable overhead

candidates.architecture: userspace application kernel/runsc intercepting system calls between workload and host kernel
candidates.harvest: stronger kernel attack-surface reduction when process sandboxing is insufficient
candidates.expectedBenefit: stronger isolation boundary for risky general-app workloads
candidates.requiredDependencies: container runtime/runsc and supported Linux host
candidates.compatibilityRisks: substantially higher setup/runtime cost and syscall compatibility considerations
candidates.upstreamIssues: not justified for ordinary Ferrum process targets without a measured isolation need
candidates.smallestExperiment: only after lighter sandbox experiment, run identical service fixture under runsc and compare compatibility/overhead
candidates.acceptanceTest: material security/capability benefit justifying higher cost with full evidence parity
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: process sandbox proves insufficient for a concrete workload

candidates.purpose: cross-platform sandbox policy for agent-executed commands
candidates.architecture: platform-specific confinement behind one runtime interface, including Linux bubblewrap/network controls and Windows/macOS policies
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: future cross-platform process isolation adapter contract
candidates.harvest: one portable policy model with platform-specific enforcement and explicit Windows hardening patterns
candidates.expectedBenefit: avoid hard-coding Ferrum isolation around one Linux implementation
candidates.compatibilityRisks: experimental project and heterogeneous platform guarantees
candidates.upstreamIssues: must independently prove every platform rather than infer parity from one backend
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: current head includes live-tested Windows non-interactive logon hardening
candidates.smallestExperiment: map Ferrum's desired isolation contract to its portable policy model without product dependency
candidates.acceptanceTest: contract can express equivalent filesystem/network/process restrictions with truthful capability discovery
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Ferrum adopts any first isolation adapter

challenge.reason: No workflow-security, dependency-integrity or sandbox candidate has yet completed an identical-workload Ferrum experiment. The only product proposal remains the exact Node 24.19.0 pin, and it remains off main while one Tauri Ubuntu reference job is still running.

nextExperiments: Finish PR59 exact-head Tauri proof; merge only if every required workflow is completed success and main remains compatible.
After any newer product merge, refresh PR60 onto current main; verify durable STATUS synchronization on the final exact head with automatic npm caching explicitly disabled.
Run lockfile-lint against canonical package-lock plus planted wrong-host, insecure-scheme, package-name and integrity defects; compare against plain npm ci.
Run zizmor v1.29.0 and actionlint v1.7.12 against current Ferrum workflows with controlled planted defects before considering either as a permanent gate.
Then run the same Ferrum process/service workload unisolated versus strict Sandlock; benchmark nsjail/bubblewrap only if the leading result is unclear.
guardrails: No product merge while any declared exact-head acceptance workflow is incomplete.
No npm cache or node_modules cache reintroduction after run39's measured cross-platform rejection.
No sandbox is accepted based on documentation alone; requested protections must be proven active and fail closed.
No reduced browser/app/mobile/Tauri/WebDriver/evidence coverage, no hidden fallback, no caps, and no lower fidelity.
